anya: saw a p99 tail jump after the kernel-selector change last night — wondering if it's scheduler/batching related or kernel micro-behavior
sam: numbers? p95/p99 and which model/seq_len distribution
anya: p95 ~ 86ms (unchanged), p99 jumped from 220ms -> 420ms on 4k-ish requests; overall throughput ~ -5% but tail worse. model: open-llama-8k, hostdedicated cluster, GPUs: A100-80
sam: link to perf dashboard? :eyes:
anya: https://console.redwood/perf/exp/2123  (private) — quick paste of the top of profiler:
```
TAIL_SAMPLE: 2026-03-15 02:04
avg_latency: 78.9ms
p95: 86.1ms
p99: 421.7ms
kernel_fallbacks: 12.3% -> after-change
kv_cache_hit: 72% -> now 59% for long prompts
microbatch_wait_ms_hist: mode=5ms, tail>50ms
```
mike: hunch: kernel selector picked a newer matmul kernel that's slightly faster in median but worse for certain sequence length + microbatch shapes — that can increase KV cache churn and cause tails
zhang: agree. other signals: queue_delay tail increased. I'm seeing more small batches (1-3 requests) being dispatched instead of coalesced. maybe max_wait_ms param tweak or max_batch_tokens interaction
anya: can we run quick sweep: max_wait_ms=4/8/12 and max_batch_tokens=2048/4096 with kernel selector forced to old kernel vs new kernel? want to see p99 vs total tokens/sec
sam: running 3x ephemeral jobs on dedicated canary: `./bench --model open-llama-8k --load=synthetic --qdelay-sched --max_wait_ms=8 --max_batch_tokens=4096 --kernel=auto` — will post
infra-bot: deploy job started (job id jk-9012) — will notify on completion
mike: also capture KV cache trace. If microbatch shape changes, KV shard affinity can oscillate and hit rate goes down -> serializing more token work per request
anya: u/x is the kernel fallback rate in profiler? i saw a spike at tail
sam: profiler shows `fallback(kernel->slow_path)` count spiked ~+9% at the same window as p99. I'll attach callgraph snippet:
```
call: forward->matmul_opt:newkernel
    p50: 6ms
    p99: 48ms
fallback: matmul->legacy
    p50: 8ms
    p99: 210ms
```
zhang: that fallback p99 is huge — suggests some microbatches trigger a path that runs legacy kernels and kills tail. Possible small-batch shape causing kernel mismatch
anya: initial sweep results:
- (max_wait_ms=4, max_batch_tokens=2048, kernel=old): p99 230ms, throughput -8%
- (max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096, kernel=auto): p99 420ms, throughput baseline
- (max_wait_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=8192, kernel=new): p99 390ms, throughput +2%
so lowering wait reduced tail but dropped throughput. bigger batch tokens helped throughput but tails still bad when kernel=auto
mike: canonical tradeoff. to protect SLO we can bias scheduler to prefer larger microbatch shapes for seq_len >= 2k, or special-case seq_len>3k to use old kernel path until newkernel stabilizes
sam: or route requests with long prefixes to a dedicated pool with kernel=old to avoid fallback surprises — similar to routing policies we already have
anya: can we try hybrid: dynamic kernel routing by seq_len with a small grace window to avoid frequent flips? e.g., if avg_seq_len over last 30s > 2k then prefer `legacy` for that pool
zhang: yes — also look at KV prefix caching: caching the first N KV pages for long prompts brought hit rate from 59% -> 83% in a synthetic run (single worker test). That reduces repeated cache loads which were amplifying tail
mike: plan: 1) run A/B canary that forces kernel=legacy on 10% of traffic for seq_len>3k; 2) tweak scheduler: set max_wait_ms=6 for default pool to reduce microburst singles; 3) enable aggressive prefix KV prefetch for long prompts; measure token/sec and p99
anya: action items: Sam -> run canary and attach traces; Zhang -> implement temp scheduler bias flag + KV prefetch; Mike -> prepare rollback plan and perf dashboard annotations; Anya -> synth test and collect end-to-end traces
sam: starting canary now at 10% routing (canary id: rt-can-34)
infra-bot: canary deployed to pool p-can-34, monitoring p95/p99 & kv-hit-rate
anya: thanks — let's sync in 2 hours, will post intermediate numbers. if p99 not improved by 30% we fallback kernel-selector change and open PR for stricter selection policy
mike: :thumbsup:
zhang: added checklist to the ticket: https://issues.redwood/INF-2048
anya: logging results as we go. thanks team.
